hero.title: Hi, I'm Niklas.
hero.description: I make sure software isn't just built but runs reliably – with well-designed architecture, automated platforms and security by design.

bio.title: Niklas Tat
bio.content: Programming has been with me for as long as I can remember – first out of curiosity, now as my profession. For more than ten years I have been building backend systems and keeping them running reliably: designing services, breaking monoliths into microservices, automating deployments and setting up infrastructure that lets teams ship quickly and safely.
highlights: Security by design – from the architecture to the pipeline
Pragmatic and analytical: understand first, then build
Automation over manual work – recurring tasks end up in code
At home in distributed teams and productive remote work

approach.title: My Approach
approach.content: Good systems are easy to operate. That is why I think about backend and platform together: clean code, automated tests and deployments, monitoring with meaningful alerting – and an architecture that grows with the requirements.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: A selection of my work – production systems, open-source tools and side projects across backend, platform and infrastructure.

items.title: Eventfrog
items.description: Digital event management and ticketing platform.
items.extendedDescription: Eventfrog is a digital event management and ticketing solution that simplifies the entire process from publishing an event to ticket sales and admission. The platform provides the infrastructure to efficiently handle events and ticket sales.

items.title: Teamspeak Bot
items.description: Admin bot for TeamSpeak servers: protects designated groups, creates support channels automatically and ships further admin tools.
items.extendedDescription: Java-based admin bot with a modular architecture. Features include: protecting designated groups from unauthorized access, a support-channel manager that dynamically creates temporary channels per request, automatic cleanup routines, and additional admin tools. Runs as a service on the TeamSpeak host and communicates over the server-query API.

items.title: Vogeez Authorization Service
items.description: OAuth2 authorization service for registering and authenticating users.
items.extendedDescription: Spring Boot-based OAuth2 server (Authorization Code & Client Credentials flows). Persistence with PostgreSQL via Hibernate, containerized with Docker, deployed to Kubernetes via Helm. Exposes endpoints for user registration, login, token issuing and token validation. Schema updates via Hibernate migrations, test coverage with JUnit and Mockito.

items.title: Stratospheric Balloon Project
items.description: Team project: a self-built probe rode a weather balloon into the upper stratosphere and captured footage of Earth's curvature.
items.extendedDescription: Together as a team, we sent a self-built probe into the stratosphere via weather balloon to collect video footage and measurement data. Earlier launch attempts sharpened our understanding of material resilience and system reliability. The final launch succeeded: the balloon reached the upper stratosphere, the probe recorded footage of Earth's curvature and the blackness of space. After an adventurous landing, we recovered the probe and all data intact. A formative experience in applied engineering, project planning, and resilience.

items.title: Personal Portfolio Website
items.description: My personal portfolio – server-side rendered in Rust and a playground for new ideas.
items.extendedDescription: This portfolio is a Rust server-side rendered site built on Axum and Maud with a typed JSON translation catalogue, dynamically generated OpenGraph cards and a hardened multi-stage Docker image. It is published as a Helm chart whose version stays in lockstep with the binary via semantic-release. The interface is an archipelago of floating low-poly islands rendered with three.js and CC0 models by Kenney – with camera flights, switchable moods and two dogs at play.

items.title: Helm Repository
items.description: Helm chart monorepo for Kubernetes infrastructure and services.
items.extendedDescription: Centralized monorepo for Helm charts that bundles infrastructure components and production services. Charts are linted, scanned, and published to an OCI registry through GitHub Actions pipelines. Simplifies Kubernetes deployment lifecycle management with consistent versioning, shared templates, and automated publishing. Acts as the single source of truth for all self-hosted cluster workloads.

items.title: Semantic Release Action
items.description: Composite GitHub Action for automated version management and release publishing using conventional commits.
items.extendedDescription: Composite GitHub Action that parses conventional commits, automatically computes SemVer versions, generates changelogs, and creates GitHub releases. Includes fine-tuned logic for major/minor/patch bumps with [skip ci] handling, optional branch protection, and configurable scopes. Used as the central release mechanism across multiple production repositories, replacing heavyweight Node-based solutions with a lean, transparent Bash/JS implementation.

items.title: Helm Chart Action
items.description: Composite GitHub Action for the Helm chart lifecycle — scanning, linting, and OCI registry publishing.
items.extendedDescription: GitHub Action that orchestrates the full Helm chart lifecycle in CI: static linting (helm lint, kubeval), vulnerability scanning, version bumping, packaging, and pushing to an OCI registry. Provides a uniform, declarative chart-publishing workflow across repositories and reduces chart pipelines to a single workflow step. Embedded in the Helm Repository monorepo and several service pipelines.

This may include IP addresses, contact requests, meta and communication data, contact details, names, and other data generated through a website.

sections.title: 3. Content Delivery Network (CDN) via Cloudflare
sections.content:
We use the services of Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA, to increase the security and speed of our website. Cloudflare protects the website from attacks and optimizes loading times by acting as a Content Delivery Network (CDN).

For this purpose, all data traffic between your browser and our website is routed through Cloudflare's infrastructure, processing your IP address and other usage data. Data transfer to the USA is possible. Cloudflare is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which ensures an adequate level of data protection. Usage is based on our legitimate interest in a secure and performant website.

sections.title: 4. Local Storage and Cookies
sections.content:
This website does not set any cookies itself and does not use any analytics or tracking services. If you select a colour mood, this choice is stored exclusively in your browser (local storage) so that it persists on your next visit. This information is not transmitted to us and can be deleted at any time via your browser settings.

Cloudflare may set technically necessary cookies to protect against attacks (e.g. “__cf_bm”). These serve solely the security of the website and contain no information about your usage behaviour. You can block or delete cookies and site data in your browser at any time.

sections.title: 8. SSL/TLS Encryption

You can recognize an encrypted connection by the address line of the browser changing from "http://" to "https://" and by the lock symbol in your browser line.
